title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, taken from the surrounding pages. G is the group generated by rho (order 6), sigma (order 4) and tau (an involution), with rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. It is essentially GL(2,Z), with G^+ = SL(2,Z), and the hat denotes profinite completion. Pi = Gamma^+[2] = Ker(SL(2,Z) -> SL(2,Z/2)). This is a central extension (15) of pi_{0,3} = pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,infinity}), a free group on two generators, by mu = {±1}. The splitting (16) sends the loop l_i to lambda_i = -l_i. It is legitimate because l_inf l_1 l_0 = -1. Pi_0 is the subgroup generated by the lambda_i. On the previous page Grothendieck showed that Pi_0 has index 2 in Pi and is normalized by rho, sigma and tau, hence by G, and therefore that its completion Pi_0^ is normalized by G^.

This page finishes part (b) of that Proposition: Pi_0^ is normalized by the whole group M. Here M is a 'Teichmüller-type' group of automorphisms of G^ (or G^{+^}) attached to the loop equation. It decomposes as M = M(0)·G^{+^}, where G^{+^} acts by inner automorphisms and M(0) ≅ M~_{0,3}(0). Inner automorphisms preserve Pi_0^ because it is normal in G^, so it suffices to treat u in M(0).

Such a u is described by (20):
- u(rho) = int(alpha) rho;
- u(sigma) = eps_2(mu) int(beta) sigma, with eps_2(mu) a sign depending on mu;
- u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu, with mu in Z^*.

This is a GT-like parametrization: mu plays the role of the cyclotomic character, and alpha, beta are conjugating elements. The steps are:
1. From (20), u(l_0) = l_0^mu. Since -1 is central and fixed, and (-1)^mu = -1 for mu odd (a unit of Z^), we get u(lambda_0) = u(-l_0) = (-l_0)^mu = lambda_0^mu, which lies in Pi_0^.
2. Since lambda_1 = rho(lambda_0), conjugation by rho, we have u(lambda_1) = (u rho u^{-1})(u(lambda_0)) = (alpha rho alpha^{-1})(lambda_0^mu). This lies in Pi_0^ because Pi_0^ is normal in G^.
3. lambda_inf = (lambda_1 lambda_0)^{-1} is then automatic. Since Pi_0^ is topologically generated by lambda_0 and lambda_1, u(Pi_0^) is contained in Pi_0^.

Corollary (22): Pi ≅ Pi_0 × mu and Pi^ ≅ Pi_0^ × mu, where mu = {±1} = Centre(G^{+^}). This is immediate, because Pi_0 is the image of a group-theoretic section of the central extension (15). The point of the whole page is to obtain a canonical complement Pi_0^ ≅ pi^_{0,3} inside Pi^. This complement is stable under the full 'Teichmüller' group M, so the action of M on pi^_{0,3} can be read off. This prepares the normalization of alpha and beta modulo mu on the next page, with alpha in Pi_{0,tau} and beta in Pi_0.
errors: The final line writes u(lambda_1) ∈ Pi_0. It should be Pi_0^ (profinite completion).
'nécessaire et suffisant' is fine but the 'necessary' part is idle; only sufficiency is used. Inner automorphisms by G^{+^} preserve Pi_0^ because Pi_0^ is normal in G^ (previous page).

Implicit step: u(l_0) = l_0^mu is deduced from u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu. This presupposes that l_0 is identified with eps_0, or with a conjugate of it compatible with the chosen normalization. That identification is not written on this page.
Implicit step: u(-1) = -1, because -1 generates the characteristic centre. This is needed to pass from u(l_0) to u(-l_0) and is used without comment.

ideas.what: Gamma(2) = Ker(SL2(Z)->SL2(Z/2)) as a central extension of the free group pi_{0,3} by ±1. It has a section l_i -> -l_i whose image Pi_0 is normal in GL2(Z), giving Gamma(2) ≅ F_2 × {±1}.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting Gamma(2) = {±1} × F_2; P^1 - {0,1,inf} as the level-2 modular curve (Legendre family)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th c. modular function theory; Sanov's theorem for free subgroups)
ideas.where_published: Not as such. La Longue Marche discusses the modular tower and level structures in general terms.

ideas.what: Parametrization of the automorphisms u of the profinite modular group by (mu, alpha, beta): u(rho) = int(alpha) rho, u(sigma) = eps_2(mu) int(beta) sigma, u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu.
ideas.modern_name: GT-hat-type action on the profinite completion of SL2(Z)/GL2(Z) (genus 1 / M_{1,1} part of the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches Galois action on the Teichmüller tower, including M_{1,1}, without these formulas.

ideas.what: Stability of the canonical complement Pi_0^ ≅ pi^_{0,3} under the whole automorphism group M, via the parity argument (-1)^mu = -1.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the GT action on F^_2 with that on the profinite modular group through the level-2 cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura's work on Galois action on Gamma_{1,1}

missed.claim: This is an explicit early (pre-Drinfeld) treatment by Grothendieck of the profinite modular group G^ and its 'Teichmüller' automorphism group M. M has decomposition M = M(0)·G^{+^}, cyclotomic parameter mu, and a sign eps_2(mu) on the order-4 generator. It is related to pi^_{0,3} via a canonical, M-stable complement of the centre in Gamma(2)^. The individual mathematics is now standard (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). What matters historically is that the genus-1 / level-2 compatibility was already being set up here. The sign eps_2(mu) normalization is a small detail worth comparing with later conventions.
missed.quote: u(sigma) = eps_2 int(beta) sigma ... u(-l_0) = (-l_0)^mu i.e. u(lambda_0) = lambda_0^mu (car (-1)^mu = -1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's own route to GT-type actions on SL2(Z)^ via the level-2 cover, before the published GT literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification: a normal subgroup is preserved by an automorphism group, plus a trivial corollary about a split central extension. The context (GT-like automorphisms of the profinite modular group) is historically interesting but matches later published work.
transcription_corrections: In the corollary (22), the image reads 'Pi ≃ Pi_0 × mu' (bold or underlined Pi) and '\hat{Pi} ≃ Pi_0^ × mu'. It is Pi, not lower-case pi.
In the side conditions of (20), the image seems to read 'beta ∈ \hat{Pi}' rather than '\hat{pi}'.
The braced annotation under (u rho) reads 'ad(int(alpha) rho) u', i.e. u rho u^{-1} = int(alpha) rho.
The final line should read u(lambda_1) ∈ Pi_0 (as written), meaning Pi_0^.

The bracketed remark after the corollary reads roughly: 'C'est trivial, puisque Pi_0 = un scindage de l'extension centrale (15)'. This replaces the crossed-out 'Il suffit de remarquer que l'élément -1 n'est pas dans Pi_0'.
